sentences.text:
The applications are filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short,
'Code'), for orders of pre-arrest bail.

2. B.A. Nos.1059/2024 and 1237/2024 are filed by the accused 2 and 4 in Crime No.102/2024, B.A.
Nos.1205/2024 and 1242/2024 are filed by the accused 2 and 4 in Crime No.104/2024, B.A.
Nos.1202/2024 and 1233/2024 are filed by the accused 2 and 4 in Crime No.107/2024 and B.A.
Nos.1206/2024 and 1243/2024 are filed by the accused 2 and 4 in Crime No.109/2024 BAIL APPL.

NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES all of the Koipuram Police Station, Pathanamthitta,
registered against the accused (four in number) for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 409 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 5, 23, 3 and 21 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (in short, 'BUDS Act').

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As the petitioners are the same in the above crimes and the crimes arise out of similar transactions, the applications are consolidated, jointly heard and are being disposed of by this common order.

B.A.
No.1205/2024 is treated as the leading case.

3. The common case of the defacto complainants in all the above crimes, in brief, is that: they had deposited money in an establishment named PRD Finance, managed by the accused 1 to 4, on the false promise made by the accused that they would pay high rate of interest on their deposits.

Later,
the accused changed BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES the name of the establishment to G and G Finance.
The accused had failed to pay any interest, instead, they misappropriated the capital.
The accused have violated the regulations of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
Thus, the accused have committed the above offences.

4. Heard; Sri. P. Sreekumar, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners, Sri. C. S.
Hirthwik, Smt. Seetha S., Smt. Neema T. V., learned Public Prosecutors and Sri. D. Kishore, the learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainants/ intervenors.
5. The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners argued that the petitioners have no involvement in the crimes.

The reading of FIRs would substantiate that the defacto complainants had deposited their money in G and G Finance, which is a proprietorship concern of the first accused in the above crimes named, BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES Gopalakrishnan, who is the husband of the second accused and the father-in-law of the fourth accused.
Merely because the concern belongs to the first accused, the petitioners cannot be attributed to have committed the offences.
The petitioners are law abiding citizens and are women.
It is without verifying the records that the Police have implicated the petitioners as accused in the crimes.
In any given case, the petitioners' custodial interrogation is not necessary and no recovery is to be effected.
The petitioners are willing to co-operate with the investigation and abide by any stringent condition that may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, the applications may be allowed.

sentences.text: The learned Public Prosecutors seriously opposed the applications.
They submitted that the petitioners have taken the innocent depositors for a ride.

The accused have deliberately started companies/ BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES concerns in different names,
which are all family concerns.
They have dishonestly offered high interest rates and collected crores of rupees from the depositors.
Later, they have consciously changed the names of the companies/concerns and cheated the depositors by siphoning off their hard earned money.
The petitioners/the accused 2 and 4 were actively involved in the day to day affairs, management and administration of the finance companies/concerns, including M/s. G and G Finance.
The petitioners have misappropriated and swindled the depositors money.
There are 380 cases registered against the petitioners in two Police Stations in Pathanamthitta district, as on today.
If the petitioners are granted an order of pre- arrest bail, they would torpedo the investigation, tamper with the evidence and intimidate the witnesses.
The petitioners custodial interrogation is necessary and BAIL APPL.
NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES recovery is to be effected.
The accused 1 and 3 have already been arrested and are in judicial custody.
Hence, all the applications may be dismissed.
7. The learned counsel for the defacto complainants/intervenors also strenuously opposed the applications.
In B.A. No.1205/2024, the defacto complainant has filed a counter affidavit,

wherein,
he has produced certain documents to substantiate that the defacto complainant had deposited the money in PRD Finances on 20.10.2020.

He also drew the attention of this Court to Annexure R2(b)
document to demonstrate that the second accused was a director of the PRD Financiers Private Limited.
Subsequently, the second accused submitted Annexure R2(c) document on 07.05.2019 tendering her resignation from the directorship of PRD Nidhi Limited.
Thereafter, the directors of PRD Financiers Private Limited had BAIL APPL.
NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES submitted a letter to the RBI to change the name of PRD Financiers Private Limited.

However, the RBI by letter dated 06.02.2020, rightly figured out that, as the three entities namely, PRD Financiers, PRD Chitty Funds India Private Limited and PRD Nidhi Limited, were owned by the same family, doing business in financial activities under a common brand name 'PRD', the change of the name would cause confusion among the general public.

entities.text: PRD Chitty Funds India Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, the RBI, by Annexure R2(e), permitted PRD Financiers Private Limited to change its name to Pullad Finance Private Limited.
The second accused is a director of the said company also.

Subsequently, on 31.03.2022,
the fourth accused was inducted as a director.
The accused 2 and 4 are continuing as directors of the company as evidenced by Annexure R2(i) document dated 30.09.2022.
Annexure R2(k) public notice was published that PRD Financiers BAIL APPL.
& CONNECTED CASES Private Limited is now functioning as G and G Finance.

The defacto complainant has specifically stated in his complaint lodged with the Police that the accused, who are the directors of PRD Financiers Private Limited, have deliberately changed the name to G and G Finance, to hoodwink the public.
The materials on record undoubtedly substantiate that the accused have started finance companies in different names, which is a family business, to cheat their depositors and the general public.
There are 380 cases registered against the accused in two Police Stations, for cheating the depositors.
The petitioners are influential persons.
If they are granted orders of pre-arrest bail, they would certainly flee from justice and sabotage the investigation.

The learned counsel relied on the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagan Mohan Reddy Y. S. v. Central Bureau of BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES Investigation [2013 KHC 4402] and Chidambaram P.V. v. Directorate of Enforcement [2019 KHC 6886] and a decision of this Court in Sindhu Nair vs State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5467590/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He prayed that the applications may be dismissed.

8. The gravamen of the prosecution allegation is that, the accused 1 to 4 had started different family concerns/companies and received deposits from the public, without any license or permission, by offering high rates of interest.
The accused deliberately changed the names of the companies/concerns to cheat the depositors and misappropriated their deposits.

9. The cardinal contention of the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners is that, the accused 2 and 4 BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES have no involvement in the concern named G and G Finances, which is a proprietorship concern of the first accused, husband of the second accused and the father- in-law of the fourth accused.
Therefore, the petitioners cannot be roped in as accused in the crimes.

10. The learned Public Prosecutors as well as the counsel for the defacto complainants have refuted the submission by contending that the accused have consciously started companies/concerns in different names with the sole intention to cheat their depositors.
All the companies and concerns have been managed and administrated by the accused as family business.
They have in furtherance of their common intention cheated all their depositors.
All the establishments of the accused were functioning without obtaining any permission or sanction in contravention of the provisions of the BUDS Act.
BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES 11.

In Jagan Mohan Reddy Y.S. v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2013 KHC 4402] case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically declared that economic offences constitute a separate class and need to be visited with a different approach when it comes to the question of bail.

entities.text: Jagan Mohan Reddy Y.S. v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2013 KHC 4402]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The economic offences having deep-rooted conspiracies and involving huge loss of public funds need to be viewed seriously and be considered as grave offences affecting the country's economy as a whole.

12. In Himanshu Chandravadan Desai and others v. State of Gujarat [2006 (2) SCC (Cri) 143] the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the Courts should be circumspect and cautious in granting aniticipatory bail in crimes involving a conspiracy to cheat and defraud public institution in a systematic manner.

entities.text: Himanshu Chandravadan Desai and others v. State of Gujarat [2006 (2) SCC (Cri) 143]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES 13.

In Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another, [(2012) 4 SCC 379] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has reiterated the legal position that, an order of pre-arrest bail being an extra ordinary privilege, should be granted only in exceptional cases.

entities.text: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another, [(2012) 4 SCC 379]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judicial discretion conferred upon the Courts has to be properly exercised, after proper application of mind, to decide whether it is a fit case to grant an order of pre-arrest bail.
The court has to be prima facie satisfied that the applicant has been falsely enroped in the crime and his liberty is being misused.

sentences.text:
In P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement [(2019) 9 SCC 24], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in the following lines:
"69.

entities.text: P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement [(2019) 9 SCC 24]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ordinarily, arrest is a part of procedure of the investigation to secure not only the presence of the accused but several other purposes.
Power under Section 438 CrPC is an extraordinary power and the same has to be BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES exercised sparingly.
The privilege of the pre- arrest bail should be granted only in exceptional cases.

The judicial discretion conferred upon the court has to be properly exercised after application of mind as to the nature and gravity of the accusation; possibility of the applicant fleeing justice and other factors to decide whether it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Grant of anticipatory bail to some extent interferes in the sphere of investigation of an offence and hence,
the court must be circumspect while exercising such power for grant of anticipatory bail.

Anticipatory bail is not to be granted as a matter of rule and it has to be granted only when the court is convinced that exceptional circumstances exist to resort to that extraordinary remedy."
15.
The materials placed on record, prima facie show that the accused had initially started the finance business as PRD Finance.
Then, the company PRD Financiers Private Limited was incorporated.
The name of the company was later changed to Pullad Finance Private Limited.

Then,
the first accused has allegedly started G and G Finance.
Indisputably, the accused 2 and 4 are the directors of the Pullad Finance Private BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES Limited, which is a continuation of the PRD Financiers Private Limited.

entities.text: Pullad Finance Private BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 16. On a prima facie appreciation of the materials, it can be deciphered that the family of the accused have conducted finance business in different names and styles and received deposits from the public without any permission or authority.
The defacto complainants have specifically alleged in the FIRs that the petitioners were in charge of the affairs of the finance business and have cheated them by misappropriating their deposits.
The veracity and genuineness of the prosecution as well as the defence are matters that are to be investigated and found out.
It is not for this Court to conduct a thread bare enquiry and render a finding on the said points at this stage.
Nonetheless, the materials on record prima facie show the active involvement of the petitioners in the family business.
BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES 17

. After bestowing my anxious consideration to the facts, the rival submissions made across the Bar, the materials placed on record, and on comprehending the nature, seriousness and gravity of the economic offences alleged against the petitioners, that the petitioners' custodial interrogation is necessary and the recovery is to be effected, I am convinced that the petitioners have not made out any exceptional grounds to invoke the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Section 438 of the code.
Therefore, the petitioners are not entitled to orders of pre-arrest bail, as it would sabotage the investigation and would have a deleterious impact on the society.
Resultantly, the bail applications are dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts: The accused have violated the regulations of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The reading of FIRs would substantiate that the defacto complainants had deposited their money in G and G Finance, which is a proprietorship concern of the first accused in the above crimes named, BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES Gopalakrishnan, who is the husband of the second accused and the father-in-law of the fourth accused.
Merely because the concern belongs to the first accused, the petitioners cannot be attributed to have committed the offences.
The petitioners are law abiding citizens and are women.
It is without verifying the records that the Police have implicated the petitioners as accused in the crimes.
The learned counsel relied on the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagan Mohan Reddy Y. S. v. Central Bureau of BAIL APPL. NO.1059 OF 2024 & CONNECTED CASES Investigation [2013 KHC 4402] and Chidambaram P.V. v. Directorate of Enforcement [2019 KHC 6886] and a decision of this Court in Sindhu Nair vs State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5467590/
9
All the companies and concerns have been managed and administrated by the accused as family business.
All the establishments of the accused were functioning without obtaining any permission or sanction in contravention of the provisions of the BUDS Act.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In Jagan Mohan Reddy Y.S. v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2013 KHC 4402] case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically declared that economic offences constitute a separate class and need to be visited with a different approach when it comes to the question of bail.
12. In Himanshu Chandravadan Desai and others v. State of Gujarat [2006 (2) SCC (Cri) 143] the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the Courts should be circumspect and cautious in granting aniticipatory bail in crimes involving a conspiracy to cheat and defraud public institution in a systematic manner.
The judicial discretion conferred upon the Courts has to be properly exercised, after proper application of mind, to decide whether it is a fit case to grant an order of pre-arrest bail.
The court has to be prima facie satisfied that the applicant has been falsely enroped in the crime and his liberty is being misused.
Sindhu Nair vs State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5467590/
10 14.
16. On a prima facie appreciation of the materials, it can be deciphered that the family of the accused have conducted finance business in different names and styles and received deposits from the public without any permission or authority.
The defacto complainants have specifically alleged in the FIRs that the petitioners were in charge of the affairs of the finance business and have cheated them by misappropriating their deposits.
The veracity and genuineness of the prosecution as well as the defence are matters that are to be investigated and found out.
It is not for this Court to conduct a thread bare enquiry and render a finding on the said points at this stage.
Nonetheless, the materials on record prima facie show the active involvement of the petitioners in the family business.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the petitioners are not entitled to orders of pre-arrest bail, as it would sabotage the investigation and would have a deleterious impact on the society.
Resultantly, the bail applications are dismissed.
